title: Russian strike kills nine in Dymer near Kyiv as drone attacks hit Russian ships off Finland and Libya
dek: At least 12 people were killed across the Kyiv region overnight and 11 are missing in Dymer. Finland says Ukraine likely hit a Russian military cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland; a Russian corvette was struck at Benghazi.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A Russian drone strike on a five-storey apartment block in Dymer, a town about 45 km north of Kyiv, killed at least nine people, and rescuers were still searching the rubble on Monday morning for 11 people, including two children, Ukrainian officials said. Overnight attacks across the Kyiv region killed at least 12 people in all, according to the region's military administration, and the region declared Monday a day of mourning.

The strike came during a weekend in which the war spread visibly beyond Ukraine's borders. A Russian cargo ship serving the Russian defence ministry was set on fire by drones in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, and on Sunday a Russian navy corvette was hit by suspected sea drones while docked at Benghazi in Libya, according to Finnish and Libyan officials. Ukraine has not claimed either attack. NATO allies are due to meet in Brussels on Monday after Polish prosecutors said three objects that fell on Polish soil on Friday were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles.

## What happened in the Kyiv region

The Dymer building was hit overnight into Sunday. On Sunday morning, Tymur Tkachenko, head of the Kyiv regional military administration, said the building had been "destroyed" and that two people were injured. The toll rose through the day as rescuers dug through the collapsed section: Ukraine's State Emergency Service said by Sunday evening that two people had been killed, including an 18-year-old, and that it was searching for 11 people who were "not responding or cannot be reached". Early on Monday Mr Tkachenko said the toll in Dymer had reached nine, after another body was recovered, according to reports. The dead include a teenager and a woman in her forties, he said. A child was pulled out alive on Sunday evening, reports said.

Figures changed several times overnight and reports gave different counts at different hours; the toll is provisional and could rise.

Elsewhere in the region, a strike on a supermarket in Vyshneve killed two people and wounded eight, and a strike on a private house in Bila Tserkva killed one person, according to reports citing regional officials. "People had simply gone to the store to buy groceries," Mr Tkachenko said. Ukraine's Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said a power substation in the Dnipropetrovsk region was also hit.

Ukraine's air force said 161 of the 186 drones Russia launched overnight into Sunday had been shot down or jammed. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had launched about 2,700 drones, nearly 1,460 aerial bombs and 165 missiles at Ukraine over the past week, and urged the United States to approve delayed transfers of Patriot air-defence missiles, according to reports. In Odesa, where strikes damaged the main power grid, schools will teach remotely from 23 to 27 November.

Russia's defence ministry did not comment on the Kyiv region strikes. It said on Sunday that its air defences had shot down 792 Ukrainian drones in 24 hours and that its forces had captured the village of Sosnovy Bor in the Kharkiv region. Ukraine's military said separately that its forces had retaken 204 square km and 14 settlements north and north-east of Velykyi Burluk in the same region. Neither side's battlefield claims could be independently verified.

## The war at sea

The cargo ship Sparta II, 121 metres long, caught fire after a drone strike on Saturday while sailing from St Petersburg to the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. The Finnish Defence Forces said it was hit in international waters west of Gogland Island and then drifted into Finnish waters, and that the strike was likely carried out by Ukraine. Its 16 crew were taken off by a nearby Russian ship. The vessel is owned by Oboronlogistika, a company that provides logistics for Russia's defence ministry, and is under US Treasury sanctions, according to reports.

"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finland's Prime Minister Petteri Orpo wrote on X, adding that "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor." President Alexander Stubb said the burning ship posed a "serious danger" in Finnish waters. Finland reimposed temporary air and sea restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland and informed NATO, reports said. The ship later left Finnish territorial waters.

On Sunday, Libyan military officials said two sea drones hit the Russian corvette Merkury at the Benghazi naval base and at least four more were intercepted, according to reports. Libya's eastern-based authorities said the ship had stopped to refuel and resupply under a maritime cooperation agreement with Russia, and that they had opened a joint investigation with Moscow. Reports differ on how badly the ship was damaged. Hours later, a second vessel, reportedly flagged in Malta, was hit off Benghazi; its crew were rescued with minor injuries.

## Background

Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine is in its fifth year. Since the autumn Moscow has intensified nightly drone and missile attacks on Ukraine's power grid as temperatures fall towards freezing. Ukraine has stepped up long-range strikes on Russian oil and military targets, and over the past two weeks has been accused of hitting Russian ships far from the Black Sea: Finland said it detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland on 11 November.

On Friday, objects fell in eastern Poland. Polish prosecutors said on Sunday they were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles, and Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the incident an "intentional provocation" by the Kremlin. Poland has asked NATO allies for more air-defence support.

The attacks come as Washington tries to restart peace talks. Mr Zelensky said last week that he had agreed to a US plan for three-way talks with Russia before Christmas. No date or venue has been announced.

## Why it matters for India

India has consistently called for an end to the war through dialogue and diplomacy. Attacks on shipping in the Baltic and the Mediterranean raise war-risk insurance costs for vessels using those routes, and any widening of the conflict to NATO territory would add to pressure on oil and freight prices that India, which imports most of its crude, is exposed to. A fresh push for talks before Christmas would be the first serious test of whether the US-backed track can hold.

## What happens next

- Monday: rescue work continues in Dymer; the Kyiv region observes a day of mourning.
- Monday: NATO allies meet in Brussels on the Kh-101 missiles that fell in Poland.
- Libyan and Russian investigators are examining the Benghazi attacks.
- The US is working towards three-way talks with Ukraine and Russia before Christmas; no date has been set.
